messages:
Maya Chen: Quick async question — I'm wiring up error -> exception mapping in the Go client. Two quick things:
1) preferred canonical exceptions for 401/403/429/5xx?
2) best practice for surfacing request ids in logs for streaming reconnect attempts?

Code snippet I'm playing with:
```go
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
if err != nil {
    // currently returning raw http error
}
```

Jonathan Park: For (1) keep it small & actionable: AuthError (401), PermissionError (403), RateLimitError (429, expose RetryAfter), and TransientError for most 5xx (Retryable=true). Also Distinct ValidationError for 400 vs generic ClientError. That lets callers decide retry/backoff.

Rachel Li: For streaming, treat `io.EOF` vs server-terminated errors differently. EOF after some tokens => OK (stream finished). If you see connection reset or 5xx mid-stream, surface a StreamTransientError with the last good offset so client can attempt resume if supported.

Sam O'Neill: Logging: always log a request id at INFO/DEBUG. Use the X-Request-Id header when present, fallback to generated short UUID. Never log full prompt text by default — provide `REDWOOD_SDK_LOG_PROMPT=true` opt-in for devs. Example log line:
```
INFO  client.go:120 request_id=3f2a-... event="stream_reconnect" model="v1" last_offset=124 tokens=32
```

Maya Chen: Nice. Should we attach the request id to every exception object as `.RequestID`? That would help error handlers correlate logs+errors.

Jonathan Park: Yes, include RequestID string field on error types and implement `Error()` to include a short token. Also make sure the SDK exposes `Error.IsRetryable()` boolean (or `Retryable()` method) so code can act.

Rachel Li: On mapping specifics:
- 400 -> ValidationError (non-retry)
- 401 -> AuthError (non-retry, refresh token hint)
- 403 -> PermissionError (non-retry)
- 404 -> NotFoundError (non-retry)
- 409 -> ConflictError (depends)
- 429 -> RateLimitError (retryable, include RetryAfter)
- 5xx -> TransientError (retryable)
- Network timeouts -> TransientError (retryable)

Include the raw status code and any server-provided error type string on the mapped exception for observability.

Sam O'Neill: For streaming reconnect resume: add `LastEventID`/`LastTokenOffset` in error metadata. If server returns `x-resume-supported: true`, client should retry with `resume_offset`. FWIW PR is here: https://github.com/redwood/clients/pull/842 (WIP).

sdk-ci-bot: CI passed for go/unit-tests and go/integration-tests on branch feature/err-mapping (build 4721) :white_check_mark:

Maya Chen: Awesome. One last thing — debug logs for SDK internals should be gated by `REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=true`. When enabled, we can print headers (with redaction) and retry/backoff decisions. Example env var docs link: https://internal.redwood.dev/sdk/config#debug

Rachel Li: Also suggest adding a small helper in all client libs: `WrapHTTPError(resp, body)` that reads headers, maps codes, extracts `x-request-id` and returns the typed error.

Jonathan Park: I'll review the PR tomorrow, @Sam please add unit tests for mapping edge cases (missing Retry-After, unknown 4xx subtype, streaming mid-5xx). :eyes:

Sam O'Neill: On it. Adding tests + a short migration note for users who relied on raw http errors. Ping me for a quick CR if you want faster turnaround. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Thanks all — I'll update the Go client to include RequestID on errors and wire debug env. Will post another short thread when PR is ready for review.
